dispositions.topic_text: Single shared canonical serialization, ordering, and digest-binding procedure for both confirmation operations
dispositions.what: As round-56 T2: one canonical encoding and digest procedure in owner_sessions (_confirmation_binding_digest), used at the step and at the submission; action, target, version, then every field of the inputs in its model's order, lists in order, absent told apart from empty; a collision-resistant cryptographic digest.
keeps:
A pending confirmation shown for one action, target, version and inputs
    is refused, and used up, when the submission carrying its value changes
    any one of them: another action, another target, another version or
    none, another value of any input, or the same list in another order
    (rule 6).
options: Use a domain-separated typed length-prefixed encoding with an order-sensitive cryptographic digest.
Use canonical JSON with fixed rules for types, absence, numbers, Unicode, object keys and array order.
Use a dedicated ordered encoder for each confirmed action.
consequences: A typed binary encoding is unambiguous but requires shared encoding machinery.
Canonical JSON is inspectable but requires complete canonicalization rules.
Action-specific encoders are explicit but duplicate logic and may drift as actions evolve.
